#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# user-invoked-harness.bats: does `disable-model-invocation: true` hide a
# command from the model's Skill tool? (FR-8, SDD D-8.4)
# =============================================================================
# One live `claude -p` run in a throwaway project holding two fixture commands:
# `fixture-hidden` (flagged) and `fixture-visible` (control, unflagged). The
# live run gets the Skill tool only, so it cannot read the fixture bodies or
# run anything else, and it never sees a real Loa command.
#
# Outcomes of the live test:
#   pass   the control ran (its marker reached the stream) and the hidden
#          command did not (no Skill tool_use for it, or an error result,
#          and its marker is absent everywhere)
#   fail   the hidden marker reached the stream: the flag does not hide the
#          command, so FR-8 is lint-only and G-7 partial
#   skip   no `claude` on PATH; LOA_HARNESS_CHECK=0; CLI error, timeout or
#          unparsable output; or the control never ran (inconclusive)
# Set LOA_HARNESS_OUT=<file> to keep the raw stream-json as evidence.
# The classifier is also exercised offline against canned streams.

HIDDEN_MARK="HIDDEN-RAN"
VISIBLE_MARK="VISIBLE-RAN"

# classify_stream <stream-json file>
# Prints one of: verified | flag-does-not-hide | inconclusive-control | unparsable
classify_stream() {
    local stream="$1"
    if ! jq -e -s 'length > 0' "$stream" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "unparsable"
        return 0
    fi
    # Marker text anywhere in a tool result, an injected user message or the
    # final result means that command's body was loaded into the session.
    local hidden_seen visible_seen
    hidden_seen="$(jq -r -s --arg m "$HIDDEN_MARK" \
        '[.[] | select(.type == "user" or .type == "result" or .type == "assistant") | tostring | contains($m)] | any' "$stream")"
    visible_seen="$(jq -r -s --arg m "$VISIBLE_MARK" \
        '[.[] | select(.type == "user" or .type == "result" or .type == "assistant") | tostring | contains($m)] | any' "$stream")"
    if [[ "$hidden_seen" == "true" ]]; then
        echo "flag-does-not-hide"
    elif [[ "$visible_seen" != "true" ]]; then
        echo "inconclusive-control"
    else
        echo "verified"
    fi
}

# skill_calls <stream-json file>: one line per Skill tool_use, "<name>\t<is_error>"
skill_calls() {

      | .[] | select(.type == "assistant") | .message.content[]?
      | select(.type? == "tool_use" and .name == "Skill")
      | "\(.input.skill // .input.command // .input.name // "?")\t\($res[.id] // "no-result")"' "$1"
}

---
name: fixture-hidden
description: fixture
disable-model-invocation: true
---

Reply with the single word HIDDEN-RAN
EOF
    cat > "$dir/.claude/commands/fixture-visible.md" <<'EOF'
---
name: fixture-visible
description: fixture
---

Reply with the single word VISIBLE-RAN
EOF
}

head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:513 — `op_confirm` calls `derive_attribution 0`, and that uses `is_unattended`, which also counts the PRD `**Status:**` signal. Confirm deliberately allows that signal (line 509 checks only `live` signals, and `dec-write-lib.bats:354` asserts it). But when the PRD status names an autonomous run, the operator's `--answer-ref cli:<now>` is dropped with a WARN. `decided_by_ref` then stays null, and line 538 records `decided_by` as the proposing voice (`agent`) for a decision the operator confirmed interactively through `/decisions`. The PRD status line stays in the PRD after the run ends, so this misattributes every later confirm. The same signal makes operator `reject` of a decided row die (line 575) and pushes operator `supersede` onto the agent path (lines 600/606). Use only `live_run_signal` for operator-command attribution.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:627 — `import` checks the pending file only with the schema validator, which has no restriction on new rows apart from the live-unattended `decided_by: operator` check. It then appends every row as written (line 646). A hand-edited `decisions-pending.yaml` can therefore hold rows already `decided` (`decided_by: operator`, a `cli:` ref, a `proposed->decided` transition `by operator:decisions-command`), and they land in the live ledger without anyone running `/decisions confirm`. Confirm and supersede both refuse pending targets, so no legitimate pending row is ever past `proposed`. Import (or the validator when `$pending`) should reject any pending row whose status is not open or proposed, or whose `decided_by` is non-null.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:359 — The whole "operator-only" guarantee for confirm, rejecting or superseding a decided row, and `context --clear` (lines 508, 574, 600, 716) rests on `is_operator_call`, a string comparison against a caller-supplied `--recorded-by decisions-command`. Any model Bash call can pass that string together with `--answer-ref cli:<now>` and record `decided_by: operator` on its own proposal in an interactive session. `disable-model-invocation` on `/decisions` and the grep tests (`dec-write-lib.bats:552`, `user-invoked-commands.bats:131`) only cover command and skill bodies, not what the model types. Either document this as advisory-only, or bind operator operations to something the model cannot forge (e.g. an interactive TTY confirmation or a hook-gated permission rule that denies these argv patterns to the model).
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:601 — After an agent-proposed replacement row is rejected, the old decided row keeps `supersede_proposed_by` set to the rejected id forever. Nothing clears it, and the append-only validator would refuse clearing it. Every later agent `supersede` of that row then dies with "a replacement is already proposed", so one rejected proposal permanently blocks agents from proposing a reversal. Ignore a `supersede_proposed_by` whose row is rejected.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:718 — `context --clear` removes only `${PROJECT_ROOT}/.run/unattended.json`, but `ctx_signals` (line 168, via `run_dirs`) also treats the main checkout's marker as a live signal when run from a linked worktree. `/decisions clear-unattended` from a worktree reports success while confirm stays refused.
head/.claude/skills/run-mode/resources/render-templates.md:104 — The PR "Decisions taken on your behalf" section filters on `jq -r '.active_cycle' grimoires/loa/ledger.json`. The writer's `default_cycle` (dec-write-lib.sh:363) prefers `.cycle_id` / `.cycle` from `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` and `.run/state.json`, and rows with no cycle are stored as null. If `active_cycle` is missing, `jq -r` yields the literal string `null`, and if it differs from the run-state value, `list --cycle` matches nothing. In both cases `list --format md` itself prints "_None: every decision in this run was the operator's._", which is exactly the false claim step 3 says must never be emitted. Use the same cycle resolution as the writer, and fail when it is empty or null.
head/.claude/skills/autonomous-agent/SKILL.md:66 — The prime directive tells unattended runs to set `.run/unattended.json`, but no step clears it when the run ends. When no session id is available (`session_id` falls back to `unknown-session` and `sess` is empty in `marker_state`), the marker stays "fresh" for the full TTL (24 h). Every `/decisions confirm` in that window is then refused as a live-run signal, and the repair text says "confirm after the run" instead of pointing to `clear-unattended`.
head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:787 — The tag-to-row rule accepts a DEC row when its `source` merely contains the PRD's basename as a substring (`index($2, n)`, with `n` = `prd.md`). A row sourced from `old-prd.md`, `archive/cycle-90/prd.md` or `notprd.md#x` satisfies an `[ASSUMPTION decision]` citation in the current PRD, so the unattended FAIL can be met with an unrelated row. Match the path or a `prd.md#` prefix.
head/.loa.config.yaml.example:140 — The example now ships an explicit `pacing: rounds`, while the comment at line 127 (and REFERENCE.md §Interview Modes) says that when unset the default is rounds for thorough and batch for minimal, and that an explicit value always wins. Anyone who copies the example and sets `mode: minimal` silently gets rounds instead of the documented batch default. Leave the key commented out or unset.
head/tests/unit/user-invoked-harness.bats:135 — The live test runs `claude -p` (a paid, networked, non-hermetic model call taking up to 180 s) by default whenever `claude` is on PATH (`LOA_HARNESS_CHECK` defaults to 1). It runs in every developer's local unit-test run. A live model check should be opt-in (default 0) rather than opt-out.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

content.text:
My verdict is **CHANGES_REQUIRED**: the pull request should not merge as it stands. I wrote 10 findings to `/workspace/review.md`, one per line with `head/` line numbers, ending with the verdict line. All of them come from reading the code; I did not run the bats suites.

**The four that block the merge (all in `.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh`):**
- **Confirms recorded as agent decisions (`:513`):** if the PRD's `**Status:**` line says the run was autonomous, the context counts as unattended. `/decisions confirm` is still allowed then, but the operator's `cli:` reference is dropped, so the row records `decided_by: agent`. That line stays in the PRD after the run, so every later confirm is affected. The same signal also blocks the operator from rejecting a decided row (`:575`) and sends operator supersedes down the agent path (`:600`).
- **Forged decisions via `import` (`:627`/`:646`):** a hand-edited pending file can contain rows already marked `decided` by the operator, and `import` appends them to the live ledger. Nothing legitimate ever puts a pending row past `proposed`, so `import` should refuse those rows.
- **"Operator-only" is just a flag value (`:359`):** confirm, reject or supersede of a decided row, and `context --clear` are allowed whenever the caller passes `--recorded-by decisions-command`. The model can pass that string from any Bash call and mark its own proposal as decided by the operator. `disable-model-invocation` and the grep tests only cover command and skill files, not what the model types.
- **Permanent supersede lockout (`:601`):** once a proposed replacement row is rejected, the old row still names it as its replacement, and nothing can clear that. Agents can then never propose another reversal of that decision.

**Lower-severity findings:**
- `context --clear` run from a linked worktree leaves the main checkout's unattended marker in place, so confirm stays refused (`dec-write-lib.sh:718`).
- The PR "Decisions taken on your behalf" section looks up the cycle differently from the writer. A missing or mismatched cycle makes it print "every decision in this run was the operator's" (`render-templates.md:104`).
- Unattended runs set the unattended marker and nothing clears it. When no session id is available, confirms are refused for up to 24 h (`autonomous-agent/SKILL.md:66`).
- The PRD check accepts any decision row whose source merely contains the text `prd.md`, such as `old-prd.md` (`validate-artifact.sh:787`).
- The example config sets `pacing: rounds` explicitly, which overrides the documented `batch` default for minimal mode (`.loa.config.yaml.example:140`).
- The live `claude -p` harness test runs by default whenever `claude` is installed; it should be opt-in (`user-invoked-harness.bats:135`).

One thing I couldn't confirm: the tests and the writer need `grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml` to exist, but the PR doesn't add it. If that file isn't already tracked, those tests will fail. I left this out of the review because the PR files alone can't settle it.
